answer: Unique artifact custody requirement. Each agent identity must hold a distinct, non-fungible physical or computational artifact (e.g., a rare umber-dyed token) whose provenance is verified against a public ledger acting as a crystal register. Enrollment checks that no artifact is already bound to another identity, so duplicates fail. The artifact's unique signature is logged in a mirror ledger for cross-checking. An attacker must acquire genuine artifacts, one per identity, at real scarcity cost.
